decision: Origin at the study area's south-west corner, rounded down to 10 m: (299180, 5038120) in EPSG:32188. Units are metres; x east, y north, z up.
alternative: the engine converts units and handedness (Unreal: centimetres, left-handed)

decision: True north is kept. The sheets turn the map to the street grid; the game frame does not.
alternative: turn the frame to the grid, which eases level layout and loses the sun's true direction

decision: The ground is S1 as filed: 264 segments and 191 junctions, with S1's walk and car flags. G1 adds no path.
alternative: add the paths S1's checks found (canal path, park paths) as a separate, marked layer

decision: Where the 2015 surface cannot measure a building, an OpenStreetMap height is used as given (13 buildings).
alternative: none needed

decision: Where only storeys are known, height = storeys x the median height per storey of buildings of the same use that the 2015 surface measures (157 buildings; all uses 3.75 m; commerce 4.32 m from 27; industry 4.20 m from 8; residential 3.45 m from 90; services 4.11 m from 21). A use with fewer than 5 such buildings takes the median of all.
alternative: a storey height per building type and age, with more measured buildings

decision: Where nothing measures a building and S4 has no storeys, the height stays empty (14 buildings). The game must show these as unknown, never as a guessed mass.
alternative: field measurement; the 2016 3D buildings (G1b step 5)

decision: A building's door is the point of its outline closest to its access street (S4). Real entrances are not in any source used.
alternative: entrances from street photos, building by building

decision: A building is marked as having a public use when S4 places a place or an occupied commercial premise in it; 'hours known' when a place has opening hours. It marks a possible interaction. It does not say a door is open. public use, hours unknown: 123; none recorded: 115; public use, hours known: 49; vacant premises only: 9
alternative: ground-floor survey on site

decision: Every mapped object is one prop at its mapped position. A photo detection that S6 matched to a mapped object adds nothing; an unmatched one is a prop. Where one detection matches two mapped objects, or two detections one object, the count is unsure (26 groups, listed as checkpoints).
alternative: S6's own count, which keeps one prop per detection instead

decision: Each S6 kind gets a game class (config.G1_PROP_CLASS). Crossings become ground marks, road works become work zones. tree: 971; lamp: 803; crossing mark: 503; bike rack: 110; hydrant: 104; seat: 101; camera: 87; bin: 38; table: 31; work zone: 29; water: 4; shelter: 2
alternative: a finer class list

decision: An object found only in photos, and in no photo since 2023, is placed and marked possibly gone.
alternative: leave them out

decision: Road works keep the city's permit dates; the game decides when they show.
alternative: none needed

decision: The ground follows the city's 2015 terrain model, written as a 1 m grid (terrain_2015.png); every street vertex, junction, prop and outline takes its height from it.
alternative: the 2016 3D buildings' own ground; a newer terrain model

decision: Not in G1: facades, materials, interiors, canopies, private trees, what is upstairs, and the roofs of the 138 outlines the 2016 model does not cover. A game that shows them invents them, and should say so.
alternative: photo surveys, a newer 3D model

decision: A building stood on its outline in 2015 when the median height above ground inside it (surface minus terrain) is at least 2.5 m.
alternative: a different threshold; a check on aerial photos

decision: A measured height is the 90th percentile of heights above ground inside the outline, leaving out pixels within 1.0 m of its edge (walls, and misfit between sources).
alternative: the median (lower on sloped roofs) or the maximum (raised by rooftop machinery)

decision: The 2015 surface is not used for a building the roll dates 2015 or later: what it shows there is the building before. The latest year in the roll's year built counts.
alternative: aerial photos of each site

decision: The 2015 models are in NAD83(CSRS) MTM 8 (EPSG:2950), the systems in NAD83 MTM 8 (EPSG:32188). The shift between them was searched on buildings older than 2010, within 2 m in 0.5 m steps: the best fit is no shift ([0.0, 0.0]).
alternative: a published transformation grid

decision: Heights in the frame are metres above its z origin, the lowest ground in the terrain grid rounded down to a metre (3 m above sea). Where the terrain model has no triangle (outside the Sud-Ouest borough), z stays empty (16 street elements).
alternative: a terrain source for the neighbouring boroughs

decision: Each building is a separate structure set on the ground: its base is the lowest ground along its outline, so no wall floats; its top is the median ground along the outline plus its height.
alternative: a base per wall, following the slope

decision: The terrain is from 2015. Earthworks since then, such as new parks and raised streets, are not in it.
alternative: a newer terrain model, or a survey

decision: A roof face sloping less than 5 degrees is flat. A roof is flat when flat faces make 90 % of its area or more, pitched at 10 % or less, mixed between.
alternative: a finer roof typology (gable, hip, shed)

decision: The 2016 model gives a height where the 2015 surface cannot, when its parts cover at least 50% of the outline and the roll gives no year after 2016. Each part goes to the outline that holds the centre of its ground.
alternative: matching parts by overlap of their ground

decision: Between the 2016 model and the outlines no shift was found within 1 m: the median distance from a 2016 ground corner to its outline's edge is 0.752 m with no shift, and no shift lowers it.
alternative: none needed

decision: The 2016 model's own measuredHeight is 4.4 m more than its roof top above the 2015 terrain (median), so it counts from a lower ground, while its roof tops sit where the 2015 surface puts them. So Situ takes the 2016 roof top and subtracts the 2015 terrain, and keeps measuredHeight aside.
alternative: measuredHeight as given, which would add about 4.4 m to every building

decision: For the greybox the engine draws the ground flat: at z 0, with each building standing on it at its height. The 2015 terrain drawn at 1 m looked uneven and cut into buildings on slopes. The measured base, top and terrain stay in the files.
alternative: the 2015 terrain (Situ Terrain, verified)

decision: Sidewalks and islands stand 0.15 m above the flat ground: the top of the 125 to 150 mm range of the Gatineau standard (2022), a CERIU example (120 to 150 mm) and curbs seen in two walking videos. The 2015 models show they are raised (median +0.04 to +0.09 m) but are too coarse to measure a curb. Lowered curbs at crossings and driveways are not drawn.
alternative: Montreal's own standard (DTNI-3A) or a visit

decision: The greybox ground grid is turned 61.5 degrees from east, the main direction of the streets: 31% of the 22.1 km of street centrelines run within 3 degrees of it. Griffintown has other street directions (near 40 and 56 degrees), so on those streets the ground grid stays at an angle. It is a look only; no measure depends on it.
alternative: one direction per street, once road surfaces exist

decision: Where the flat ground is not street, sidewalk or building, it takes the kind OpenStreetMap gives it: green 231, play 36, plaza 56, parking 94, bike 40, water 9 pieces (rules in config.G1A_RULES). Each kind is merged first, so pieces of one kind never overlap, and a later kind in that list covers an earlier one (no two pieces drawn at the same height overlap by more than a millimetre); building outlines cut them all. Water is not walkable. Lines with no area (alleys, footways, pedestrian streets drawn as lines) are left out, so the ground there stays not classified. Each area is one outer ring: 87 holes are opened by north-south cuts (the pieces cover the same ground), and corners where an outline turns straight back are removed.
alternative: the city's park and land-use layers, once its portal is back; a visit

decision: The flat ground of the study area plus 50 m is cut into pieces (flat_ground.geojson): each piece is one kind (an area kind or not classified), no two overlap, outlines are exact to the millimetre, and pieces meet corner to corner. With building outlines and raised surfaces they cover the extent. Engines draw every piece at z 0 with one shared grid, so the areas are the ground. Two earlier ways failed (sheets laid on the ground overlapped; painting into the 1 m terrain grid gave stepped edges).
alternative: the 2015 terrain with areas draped on it, once heights return

decision: Bicycle paths (OSM highway=cycleway) lie at street level, separated by a strip or by markings (Mo, 2026-10-23), as bands: the OSM width where mapped (86), else for one-way paths the median of the mapped one-way widths (2.1 m from 59 ways), else 3.0 m for two-way paths (Ville de Montreal 2011). The city's network types four paths (about 350 m, on Wellington and near Autoroute 10) as at sidewalk level; they stay at street level here. Painted lanes on the roadway are not drawn (road markings come with road surfaces).
alternative: a visit or street photos per path
